status: source-local metadata proposal; no canonical registry, bibliography, YAML or conversion edits
primary_source: Ravi Sankar S. Nair, Tribal Languages of Kerala, Language in India 13:7 (July 2013), printed/PDF pp. 32–33

identity_evidence.claim: Glottolog 5.3 indexes this Nair 2013 work and specifically maps its Kani chapter to Kanikkaran [kev].
Kanikkaran is a separate Spoken L1 Language with glottocode kani1275, ISO 639-3 kev, and alternate names including Kanikkar/Malampashi.
Nair explicitly distinguishes the Kerala Kani speech represented in this chapter from nearby Tamil Nadu Kani speech, and lists Kerala settlement regions but no exact elicitation site.

proposed_base_language.Name: Kanikkaran
proposed_base_language.Location: Southern Kerala; Nair 2013 chapter lists regions, not an elicitation point

proposed_source_variety.Name: Kerala Kani (Nair 2013)
proposed_source_variety.Location: Kerala Kani as contrasted with Tamil Nadu Kani; broad southern Kerala chapter area only

coordinate_decision: No exact settlement among the many named places is identified as the elicitation site; leave coordinates blank rather than use a Glottolog point or an invented centroid.

transcription.source_doubled_vowels: preserve written aa/ee/uu, do not normalize to macrons in Original or claim phonemic values
transcription.source_diacritics: preserve visible underdots, underlines, tilde and breve as graphemic marks
transcription.native: blank: no Kani native-script text printed in this chapter
transcription.phonemic: blank: source does not provide separate IPA/phonemic layer

identity.reason: Source contrasts senses, grammatically inflected examples, and distinct physical pair rows; no source-stage key should disappear through same-form merging.

forms.reason: Each paired-table row and prose expression has its own physical-unit key; punctuation and double vowels are source notation, not delimiter instructions.

graph: No etymological or borrowing links are claimed by this phonological correspondence chapter; Malayalam and Tamil Nadu forms are comparisons, not asserted ancestors or donors.

bibliography.auxiliary_status: reported by Nair on p.33; uncollated and no separately ingested lexical forms
